standard_prerequisites: second-order arithmetic PA^2 and its semantic entailment
Tarski's theorem on the undefinability of truth
representability of computable functions in Q
core_obligations: Prove that no sound and complete derivation system exists for second-order logic, by reducing validity of pure second-order sentences to truth in the standard model of arithmetic and invoking Tarski's theorem
proof_roadmap: For a sentence A in the language of arithmetic, N satisfies A iff PA^2 entails A, and PA^2 entails A iff the conjunction P of its nine axioms gives a valid implication P -> A

Replace the arithmetic symbols 0, prime, +, times, < by second-order variables and universally quantify, obtaining a pure second-order sentence valid exactly when the original was valid, i.e. exactly when N satisfies A
A sound and complete proof system would enumerate the valid pure second-order sentences computably, hence the sentences true in N, contradicting Tarski's theorem that this set is not definable in Q
difficulty_reason: The argument chains three standard facts (PA^2 categoricity of truth, the symbol-elimination translation, Tarski's theorem); the source proof is complete but requires holding the reduction together.
